part.text:
Fixed. The root cause: `fcall`/`fcall_ro` carry the `CMD_SKIP_MONITOR` flag (like `eval`/`evalsha`), which suppresses the automatic MONITOR feed in `call()` (src/server.c:3435). While `eval`/`evalsha` compensate by explicitly calling `replicationFeedMonitors()` before running the script (src/eval.c:554,568), `fcallCommandGeneric` (src/functions.c:618) did not — so the `fcall` command itself never appeared in MONITOR output, only the inner commands run by the function.

The fix explicitly feeds the monitor at the start of `fcallCommandGeneric`, mirroring the eval pattern, so `fcall` is shown before the commands it executes (e.g. `[lua] "set" ...`).

Verified in the container: `unit/introspection` (includes the new "MONITOR can log commands issued by functions" test) and `unit/functions` all pass.
